documents.title: Resources and Draft Policy on Academic Integrity and AI (summary of PO 103)
documents.summary: Provost announcement summarizing the draft Academic Integrity Policy on AI (PO 103). It gives instructors the right and duty to set and communicate AI rules, requires students to cite permitted use, and warns against AI detectors.
documents.stance_why: The summary says the policy "confirms the right of the instructor to specify the permitted use of AI" and that "the faculty member holds the right to decide if/how such tools are to be used", so the university hands the decision to instructors and sets no stance itself.

units.why: The summary says the policy "confirms the right of the instructor to specify the permitted use of AI", which leaves the AI rule to each instructor, so P04 with the instructor as actor, a right (may) and no stance of its own.
units.anchor: confirms the right of the instructor to specify the permitted use of AI
units.frag_start: The policy confirms the right

units.why: The same sentence puts a duty on the instructor "to communicate permitted use of AI with the students", which is a requirement to state AI expectations, so P09 rather than P04 (the right to decide).
units.anchor: incurs the responsibility on the instructor to communicate permitted use of AI with the students
units.frag_start: The policy confirms the right

units.why: The policy "identifies certain standard tools that are, by default, acceptable for student use, unless the instructor clarifies to the contrary", which sets what applies when the instructor says nothing, so P06 (fallback) rather than P02, because the default is tool-specific and overridable.
units.anchor: standard tools that are, by default, acceptable for student use, unless the instructor clarifies

documents.title: PO 103 Appendix C: AI Tools: Sample Syllabi Language
documents.summary: Appendix C gives faculty three sample syllabus statements, from AI forbidden to allowed for some assignments to encouraged. Faculty are expected to discuss permitted AI use explicitly and may adopt or adapt the samples.
documents.stance_why: It offers three sample statements ("forbidden", "allowed in some cases", "encouraged") that faculty "may adopt / adapt", so it is a tiered template and sets no single stance.

documents.title: Generative AI Guidance (Drexel IT)
documents.summary: Drexel IT guidance on generative AI, aimed at faculty and staff, about data protection. Sensitive data must stay out of unreviewed consumer tools, approved services are covered by agreements, and new services go through a risk review.
documents.stance_why: It does not govern coursework but allows AI through approved services ("usage of approved services is governed by agreements") while barring sensitive data from unapproved tools, so permit with conditions.

units.why: The page defines generative AI as systems that "create text, images, videos, audio, and 3D models based on prompts", setting the scope of the guidance, so P61 informs.
units.anchor: uses algorithms that can create text, images, videos, audio, and 3D models based on prompts
units.frag_start: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) uses algorithms

units.why: "any university sensitive data must not be shared with any of the consumer versions of these GenAI services that have not been reviewed and approved" bans sensitive data in unvetted tools, so P50 with must-not.

units.anchor: prompts and attached files to be processed in other countries
units.frag_start: In addition to the potential for disclosure
